name: Creating an array that Contains the Numbers of Times Each Element of One Array Appears in Another Array
description: Construct a program that has a function that receives two arrays and creates an array that contains the number of times each element in the 2nd array appears in the 1st array. For example, if the 1st array is {1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6} and the 2nd array is {3, 4, 5, 6, 7}, then the array that contains the number of times each element in the 2nd array appears in the 1st array is {2, 2, 1, 1, 0}.\nAssume that all elements in the 2nd array are unique.

comments.content: This statement declares the method searchArrays that takes two arrays and creates an array that contains the number of times each element in the 2nd array appears in the 1st array

We need N variables to store the number of matches for each element in the 2nd list; that means a list is a great way to store this data. Therefore, we need to create a list with the same length as the 2nd list and fill it with 0s as we have not started counting yet. In general, the element at index i in this list will be used for storing the number of times the element at index i in the 2nd list appears in the 1st list.

This statement declares an array variable, counts, creates an array of size lst2.length, and assigns its reference to counts. By default, each number in the array is 0.
lst2.length expression returns the number of elements in the 2nd array (lst2).

We want to iterate over the indexes in the 2nd array and increment the counter that corresponds to the element at each index every time that we find a match for that element. To do this, we need use nested for loops. The outer for loop iterates over the indexes in the 2nd array while the inner for loop traverses the elements in the 1st array and increments the total number of matches for the elements in the 2nd array each time that a match is found.

This statement is the outer for loop in the nested loop that iterates over the indexes of the 2nd array.

In the first part of the loop header, we define a control variable i and initialize it to 0. In the second part of the loop header, we test whether the control variable has reached the termination threshold. The loop is repeated if the control variable is less than lst2.length and terminates when the control variable reaches lst2.length (lst2.length expression returns the number of elements in the array lst2).

In the third part of the loop header, we increment the control variable by 1 after each iteration of the loop. Note that the first part is executed once before the loop starts, the second part is executed before each iteration, and the third part is executed after each iteration of the loop.
Also note that the increment operator (++) adds 1 to the value of variable i and the result is stored back into the variable i. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement i = i + 1.

We want to iterate over the 1st array and count total number of times the elements in 2nd array appear in the 1st array. This statement is the inner for loop in the nested loop. It's a for-each statement that assigns the name val1 to each of the elements in the 1st array in turn, from left to right, and the statements inside the inner loop body will be executed for each.
We check whether the element at index i at the 2nd array and val1 from the 1st array are equal by using the == operator. The if evaluates to true if these two values are equal and false otherwise.
If the element at index i at the 2nd array is equal to val2, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.

This statement increments the counter for the element at index i at the 2nd array by 1 every time we find a match between that element and a value in the 1st array. To update the counter for the element at the index i at the 2nd array, we need to access the element at the index i of the array counts.
Each counter corresponds to one element in the 2nd array. The counter that corresponds to the element at the index i at the 2nd array has the index i.

Note that the += operator adds 1 to the value stored in counts[i] and the result is stored back into the element counts[i]. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement counts[i] = counts[i] + 1.
We want to iterate over the indexes in the 2nd array and print the total number of matches that we found for the element at each index.

In the first part of the loop header, we define a control variable i and initialize it to 0. In the second part of the loop header, we test whether the control variable has reached the termination threshold. The loop is repeated if the control variable is less than lst2.length and terminates when the control variable reaches lst2.length (lst2.length returns the number of elements in the array lst2). In the third part of the loop header, we increment the control variable by 1 after each iteration of the loop.

Note that the first part is executed once before the loop starts, the second part is executed before each iteration, and the third part is executed after each iteration of the loop.

Also note that the increment operator (++) adds 1 to the value of variable i and the result is stored back into the variable i. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement i = i + 1.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the number of matches we found for the element at index i at the 2nd array. The total number of matches for the element at index i at the 2nd array is stored in the element at index i of the array counts.

The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given string and value of the variable. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character.

We define array referred by variable values1 to hold the elements of the 1st array. We initialize the array by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in braces { }. Note that the array is of type double because we want to store floating-points numbers in the array.

We define array referred by variable values2 to hold the elements of the 2nd array. We initialize the array by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in braces { }. Note that the array is of type double because we want to store floating-points numbers in the array.
